title: Polymer sorting cards
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Making materials (9E); conservation of energy
source: Seeded from science/y9 lesson 10 (Polymer sorting cards (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 10: Polymers. To understand that polymers are long chains of monomers and how their structure gives their properties

questions.q: Is cotton a natural or synthetic polymer?
questions.model: Who made it? A plant. Made by a living thing means natural. Cotton is made of cellulose chains. So natural polymer.

questions.q: Why does a thermosoftening plastic melt when heated?
questions.a: Its chains are not cross-linked, so they can slide apart.

questions.q: Core: Sort 10 household materials into natural polymers, synthetic polymers and not polymers.
questions.a: Natural: wool, silk, cotton, paper (cellulose), rubber; synthetic: nylon, PVC, poly(ethene); not polymers: glass, steel.
questions.model: Teacher sorts two first: wool (natural polymer, protein chains), steel (not a polymer, a metal alloy).

questions.q: Extend: Explain why a carrier bag is stretchy but a milk bottle is rigid (portal response box).
questions.a: Bag: LDPE with branched, tangled chains that slide; bottle: HDPE with straight chains packed closely, stronger and stiffer.

questions.q: Stretch: Why do cross-linked polymers make good kettle bodies?
questions.a: Cross-links stop chains sliding, so they do not soften or melt when hot.

questions.q: A polymer is made of many...
Big question: what do wool, DNA and a carrier bag have in common?
questions.a: All are polymers: long chains of repeating monomers.
